NFL Win Totals Odds

NFL Win Totals are a type of NFL Futures market in which you are betting on the total number of wins an NFL team will have for the 2026 NFL season. NFL win totals represent one of the most engaging facets of sports betting, offering fans a chance to forecast a team's performance over the entire regular season. You will decide if the team will have more or less wins than what the FanDuel Sportsbook predicts. These bets can be made throughout the season, but the odds will adjust throughout the season as injuries, transactions, and other news breaks. Once your bet is placed, your wager will be settled at the end of the season.


How To Read NFL Win Totals

NFL win totals operate on an over/under basis. In the odds listed above, you’ll see two separate numbers for each team. You’ll see a number, such as 7.5, which indicates the number of wins a team is predicted to have. With this, you can either bet over if you think they'll win 8 or more games or bet under if you think they'll win 7 or fewer games during the regular season. Preseason games, Playoff games, and Regular Season Ties do not count towards the Win Total.

The second number you see will be a three digit number with a plus (+) sign or a minus (-) sign. With a plus (+) sign, a $100 bet will payout the number following the sign. For a minus (-) sign, you have to bet the number to win $100. To make your payout calculation easier, try adding picks to your betslip and we’ll do the math for you!

Betting Team Wins Over/Unders for the 2026 NFL Season

Using strategic thinking and researching can improve your chances of winning NFL win totals bets. Consider elements such as the team's previous season record, roster changes, injury updates, the strength of their schedule, and any coaching changes. Understanding these factors can provide valuable insights into a team's potential performance and significantly influence betting decisions.

NFL Win Totals Fluctuations

For much of the season, you will still be able to be on NFL Win Totals. However, the odds aren't static and will change throughout the year due to a variety of factors such as current performance, player trades, injuries, and changes in coaching staff. Staying updated with NFL news can allow you to find the most value in your win totals odds..


NFL Win Totals FAQs


  • When is an NFL Win Total wager officially graded?

    Win-total bets are settled after the league posts its official regular-season standings. FanDuel grades the market as soon as those standings are final and any league tiebreak-procedures are complete.

  • Do playoff games count toward a team’s win total?

    No—win-total markets cover regular-season games only. Post-season results (including the expanded wild-card round) never add to, or subtract from, a team’s win tally for this wager.

  • How are ties handled in Win Total bets?

    For settlement purposes, every game that finishes tied counts as a loss toward the win-total. Example: a team that goes 10-6-1 is treated as 10-7.

  • Can I cash out my win-total ticket early?

    FanDuel may offer Cash Out on certain futures. Availability is never guaranteed and can be suspended at any time; if presented, the amount shown is what you’d receive (stake + profit).

  • What if my team’s game is postponed or relocated?

    Win-total markets follow the league record, so a postponement or neutral-site switch has no direct effect. Once the NFL labels the game complete (even at a new date or venue), the outcome feeds straight into your bet.

How NFL Playoff Odds Work - Reading the “Make or Miss” Market

FanDuel Sportsbook posts two-way markets on every NFL club: Odds to Make the Playoffs and Odds to Miss the Playoffs. These are moneyline prices, so a minus sign (-) shows how much you must stake to win $100, while a plus sign (+) shows the profit on a $100 wager. Playoff odds open moments after the draft and can move after a single marquee signing or major injury. Setting up alerts on NFL news lets you pounce when numbers drift.

As an example, if you bet $160 on the Tennessee Titans to make the playoffs at -160 odds, that bet would pay out $260 (your original $160 stake and $100 in winnings). If you wagered $100 on the Miami Dolphins to make the playoffs at +118 odds, you would earn $218 (your original $100 bet and $118 in winnings).


NFL Playoff Futures FAQs


  • When does my Make Playoff or Miss Playoff bet settle?

    FanDuel settles the market as soon as the league publishes its final postseason field using the NFL’s own tiebreakers. Subsequent league appeals or statistical revisions don’t change the payout.

  • Can I cash out my playoff futures early?

    It depends. When the Cash-Out button appears, you can lock in a profit or cut losses instantly. The request isn’t guaranteed (odds can move or the market can suspend) but if it’s accepted, the offer shown is final and your bet is settled on the spot.

  • Can I combine “Make the Playoffs” odds in a parlay?

    Sure, but remember parlay rules still apply. If one leg is void (say, a team becomes ineligible because the format changes), that leg drops out and the parlay is re-priced on the remaining selections. If multiple legs become correlated because of a schedule change, FanDuel may void or resettle the ticket to keep things fair.

Super Bowl Point Spreads and Lines

Once we know which two NFL teams will play in Super Bowl 61, FanDuel Sportsbook has officially released NFL game lines and point spreads for the big game. These odds are similar to the all NFL odds seen during the regular season and throughout the NFL Playoffs.

Any favorite’s point spread is displayed with a “minus” symbol next to a whole number or a halved fraction, such as (-6) or (-6.5). Bettors picking the favorite “against the spread” must hope that the team wins by more than 6 points – a 1 through 6-point victory or a straight-up loss loses the wager. An underdog’s point spread is displayed with a “+” symbol, indicating the number of points “spotted” to the team before the Super Bowl kicks off. Underdog point-spread gamblers are hoping that the NFL team will “cover” by winning by any amount or losing by any amount smaller than the betting line. If the underdog’s point spread is (+6) and the team loses by 5 points, the bettors still win the payout.

If a game finishes with the favorites winning by the exact line margin shown on the point spread, bets are returned in an outcome known as a “push.”


Reading Super Bowl Moneyline Odds

Moneyline odds promise a % payoff when a sports bettor's chosen team wins the game straight-up. A favorite’s moneyline NFL odds are denoted with a “-“ as in (-200). Underdog moneylines are marked with a “+” as in a ML of (+350). Payoff is calculated differently for the betting odds in the favorite’s and underdog’s markets, but always centered around the value of $100.

For instance, (-150) Super Bowl odds mean that for every $150 wagered on a team, the house will pay out $100 if that team wins. (-200) odds stand for $100 payoff on every $200 wagered at the betting book. On the underdog side, moneyline odds represent the amount paid out on won $100 bets if the team surprises. (+350) odds equal a $350 payout on $100, (+1000) odds represent $1000 payout on the same risk, and so on.

How Anytime Touchdown Prop Bets Work

Anytime Touchdown scoring props only count for players who carry or catch the ball in the end zone at any point in the game. A quarterback (or other player in a trick play) who throws the ball does not count as the scorer. Only the player who catches it or runs it in will count as the Anytime Touchdown scorer. QBs are listed in the Anytime Touchdown odds because we are offering odds on that player scoring through a QB run or a trick play where the QB catches the ball.

For special teams TDs, like a kickoff or punt return touchdown, the prop will only count for the player who crosses the goal line. However, defensive touchdowns count as a Defense score for the entire unit. This includes an interception return or a fumble return touchdown.

Thanksgiving NFL Odds 2026: Spreads, Moneylines and Totals

Thanksgiving NFL odds at FanDuel Sportsbook cover a five-game holiday stretch, starting with the Packers at the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve and closing with the Broncos at the Steelers on Black Friday. The Thursday tripleheader has the Bears open as a road favorites in Detroit, the Cowboys favored at home against the Eagles, and the Bills favored over the Chiefs in prime time.

Thanksgiving NFL Schedule and Games to Watch


Packers vs Rams: Thanksgiving Eve, Wednesday, November 25

The holiday gets an early start this year. The Green Bay Packers visit the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game, streaming on Netflix at 8:00 PM ET. Both teams come in off their bye weeks, so neither side is dealing with the short turnaround the Thursday teams face.

Bears vs Lions: Thanksgiving Day, 1:00 PM ET

Football on Thanksgiving starts in Detroit, the way it has for decades. The Chicago Bears make the trip to face the Detroit Lions on CBS in the latest edition of an NFC North rivalry that has been a holiday staple for generations.

Eagles vs Cowboys: Thanksgiving Day, 4:30 PM ET

The late-afternoon window belongs to the Dallas Cowboys, and this year they host the Philadelphia Eagles on FOX. Few NFC East matchups draw a bigger holiday audience than this one.

Chiefs vs Bills: Thanksgiving night

The nightcap sends the Kansas City Chiefs to Orchard Park to take on the Buffalo Bills on NBC. It's a matchup with plenty of recent playoff history behind it, and late-November weather in Buffalo is always worth keeping an eye on when looking at the total.

Broncos vs Steelers: Black Friday, November 27

For anyone skipping the shopping lines, the Denver Broncos visit the Pittsburgh Steelers on Amazon Prime Video at 3:00 PM ET, wrapping up the holiday slate with an AFC matchup.


How to Bet on Thanksgiving Football

Every Thanksgiving week game carries the full NFL menu at FanDuel Sportsbook: point spreads, moneylines, totals, and player props, plus first-half and quarter markets. With the Thursday games running back to back from early afternoon into the night, live betting lets you follow the action between courses, with in-game lines that update throughout each matchup.

The holiday slate also lends itself to parlays. You can combine picks from different Thanksgiving games into one parlay, or build a same-game parlay (SGP) that pairs a game line with player props from a single matchup. Every leg must win for a parlay to cash, and the bet slip shows the combined odds as you add each selection.


A Short History of NFL Football on Thanksgiving

The Lions first played on Thanksgiving in 1934 and, apart from a break during World War II (1942 to 1945), have hosted a game on the holiday every year since. The Cowboys joined them in 1966 and have held the late-afternoon slot ever since, with the exception of 1975 and 1977. The NFL added a third game in prime time in 2006, and this year's schedule stretches the celebration even further with games on Thanksgiving Eve and Black Friday.


Thanksgiving NFL Odds and Betting FAQs


  • What NFL games are on Thanksgiving in 2026?

    Three games are played on Thanksgiving Day, November 26: Bears vs Lions at 1:00 PM ET on CBS, Eagles vs Cowboys at 4:30 PM ET on FOX, and Chiefs vs Bills in prime time on NBC. Packers vs Rams kicks off the week on Wednesday night, and Broncos vs Steelers follows on Black Friday.

  • Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?

    Both teams have long-standing Thanksgiving traditions. The Lions have hosted a holiday game since 1934 (except during World War II), and the Cowboys have hosted nearly every year since 1966. Their opponents rotate each season.

  • Is there an NFL game on Thanksgiving Eve?

    Yes. For the first time, the NFL is playing a game on the night before Thanksgiving, with the Packers visiting the Rams at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday, November 25, at 8:00 PM ET on Netflix.

  • Is there an NFL game on Black Friday?

    Yes. The Broncos visit the Steelers on Friday, November 27, at 3:00 PM ET, streaming on Amazon Prime Video.

  • When did the NFL start playing a Thanksgiving night game?

    The NFL added a prime-time Thanksgiving game in 2006, joining the traditional afternoon games in Detroit and Dallas to make it a three-game holiday.

  • Can I combine multiple Thanksgiving games in one parlay?

    Yes. You can add selections from any of the Thanksgiving week games to a single parlay, or build a same-game parlay using markets from one game.

How to Bet on NFL at FanDuel Sportsbook

At FanDuel, you can bet on NFL in ways that suit your strategy and level of experience. Here’s a clear beginner-to-intermediate guide on how to bet on the NFL, covering the core bet types and how to wager on the NFL at FanDuel Sportsbook.

Understanding the Main Types of NFL Bets

We offer a number of different betting markets for fans to pick from. Here are the most popular NFL bet types we offer:

  • NFL Spreads: The point spreads tries to level the playing field for both team's odds to win. A typical line might be: Chiefs -6.5 (+105) vs. Steelers +6.5 (-125). If you bet the Chiefs, they must win by 7+ points. If you back the Steelers, they can lose by 6 points—or win outright—and your bet cashes.

  • NFL Moneylines: These are the simplest form of NFL odds: pick the team you think will win outright. Favorites are denoted with a minus (-) and underdogs with a plus (+). For example: Lions -180 means you must wager $180 to win $100. Likewise, Bears +130 means a $100 bet returns $130 profit if they win.

  • NFL Totals (Over/Under): Bet on the total number of combined points in the game. If the Over/Under is set at 37.5: a 21-17 final score (38 combined points) hits the Over, while a 24-13 score (37 combined points) hits the Under.

  • Live NFL Odds (In-Game Betting): Watch and wager in real-time. Our in-play betting markets update between possessions and even between snaps. Bet on evolving outcomes like spreads, moneylines, totals, and player props as the game unfolds.

  • NFL Player Prop Bets: Target individual player stats such as passing yards for a QB, Anytime Touchdowns, rushing yards, total receptions, or interceptions. These markets are powered by official NFL data and constantly adjusted by FanDuel’s risk team to reflect real-world trends and injury status.

  • Parlays and Same Game Parlays: Combine multiple bets into a single wager for a bigger potential payout. Build your own Same Game Parlay for any NFL matchup by mixing player props, team totals, and game lines.

  • NFL Futures: Futures markets let you bet on long-term outcomes for the NFL regular season and playoffs. These include wagers such as the NFL Super Bowl winner, teams to win division titles, and which player will be crowned the NFL MVP.


Placing NFL Bets at FanDuel Sportsbook

With our website or mobile app, we make it easy to place bets on NFL events. Simply follow these steps:

  1. Sign up for a sportsbook account and veryify your ID and location if you haven't already

  2. Download the FanDuel Sportsbook app or login at sportsbook.fanduel.com on a desktop device

  3. Deposit funds

  4. Browse the NFL odds and props currently available. Click the odds to add them to your bet slip

  5. Enter a wager amount and add any promos or bonus bets you have available. The betslip will automatically calculate your potential payout. Click to place the bet when you are happy with your betslip

  6. Track your progress in the My Bets section


How to Read NFL Odds

NFL odds at FanDuel Sportsbook use the American odds format, shown as either positive (+) or negative (−) numbers:

  • +200: Wager $100 to win $200 (underdog).
  • -150: Wager $150 to win $100 (favorite).

Example: If you bet $100 on the Detroit Lions +200, you’d receive $300 total if they win: $200 in profit plus your $100 stake. Betting Philadelphia Eagles at −150 requires risking $150 to profit $100. FanDuel’s bet slip automatically calculates your payout, helping you make informed, fast decisions.


Why FanDuel is Trusted for NFL Betting


  • Trusted Market Leader: Official betting partner of the NFL.
  • Real-Time Odds: Adjusted by in-house analysts and informed by live market activity.
  • Flexible Markets: From player props to live Same Game Parlays and Super Bowl futures.
  • Responsible Gaming Tools: Deposit limits, timeouts, and support always available.

NFL Odds and Betting FAQs


  • Do overtime periods count for my NFL spread, moneyline, and totals wagers?

    Yes. FanDuel grades almost every NFL game market—including full-game spreads, moneylines, and over/unders—on the final official score after all overtime periods are completed, unless the market header specifically says otherwise.

  • What happens if an NFL game ends in a tie?

    If the final score is tied after overtime, moneyline wagers are void and stakes are refunded, while point-spread and totals bets are settled on the posted numbers (so a spread that lands exactly on the closing line is graded as a push).

  • What happens if an NFL game is postponed or moved to a different stadium?

    When a game is postponed before kickoff, all wagers are void. If it’s relocated but still played on the scheduled date—whether to a neutral site or the opponent’s stadium—bets remain live because FanDuel grades action on the official league box score, not the venue.

  • How does FanDuel treat a Same Game Parlay if one NFL leg is void (for example, because the game ended in a tie)?

    If a leg is voided, the parlay is re-priced to the odds of the remaining legs and still stands. Only when every leg in the SGP is void does FanDuel return the entire stake.
